stem: What is an accessory pathway in the pathophysiology of supraventricular tachycardia?

options.text: An extra muscle bundle that bridges the insulating fibrous layer between the atria and ventricles
A specialised part of the His-Purkinje system that speeds up normal conduction
A backup pacemaker located in the ventricular myocardium
A blockage within the AV node that forces electricity through the atria
An inflammatory scar that permanently prevents AV nodal conduction

explanation: Accessory pathway: an extra muscle bundle that bridges the insulating fibrous layer between the atria and ventricles. This is because this abnormal electrical connection bypasses the normal insulating separation and can allow re-entry circuits that cause SVT.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because an accessory pathway is an abnormal extra muscular connection between the atria and ventricles that bypasses the insulating fibrous tissue.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because the His-Purkinje system is part of the normal conduction pathway, not an abnormal bridging connection.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a backup pacemaker generates impulses; an accessory pathway conducts impulses between chambers.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because an accessory pathway is an extra route, not an AV nodal blockage.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because scar tissue may impair conduction, but it does not describe an accessory pathway.

source.hint: Think of it as an unintended electrical bridge between two chambers.
